title: Critical polynomial norms attain their infimum on tame rational analytic fields
statement: All fields below are fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values. For such a field $A$, write $A^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ for its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde A=A^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_A=|A^\times|$. For a finite extension $B/A$ set $e(B/A)=[\Gamma_B:\Gamma_A]$, $f(B/A)=[\widetilde B:\widetilde A]$ and $d(B/A)=[B:A]/(e(B/A)f(B/A))$. Call it immediate if its value group and residue field equal those of $A$, unramified if $e=d=1$ and the residue extension is separable, and tame if $d=1$, its residue extension is separable and its ramification index is prime to the residue characteristic (with no index restriction in residue characteristic zero). A field extension is separable if every algebraic element has a minimal polynomial with distinct roots. Let $k$ be complete and algebraically closed, let $z\notin k$ lie in a complete extension, and let $K=k(z)^\wedge$ denote the closure of the subfield generated by $k$ and $z$. Assume either $\operatorname{trdeg}(\widetilde K/\widetilde k)=1$ and $\Gamma_K=\Gamma_k$, or $\widetilde K=\widetilde k$ and $\dim_{\mathbf Q}((\Gamma_K/\Gamma_k)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q)=1$. Let $L/K$ be finite tame and suppose $p=\operatorname{char}(\widetilde k)>0$. For $a,b\in L$ set $s=\inf_{c\in L}|c^p-ac+b|$. If $s>0$ and $|pb|<s$, there exists $c_0\in L$ such that $|c_0^p-ac_0+b|=s$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.2(i), pp. 37–38, and type 2/3 clause of Proposition 6.2.4, p. 42, proved pp. 47–48. The former identifies the unrestricted polynomial infimum with the critical coset infimum.

proof.text: The value group of $L$ is nondiscrete: for $h\in k$ with $0<|h|<1$, algebraic closedness gives elements with norms $|h|^{1/m}$ for every $m\ge1$, tending to $1$ from below. The finite-extension calculus gives completeness of $L$. Apply the critical-coset calculus to $C=b+S_{a,s}(L)$: the assumed unrestricted infimum and $|pb|<s$ make $C$ critical.

Apply coefficient normalization with $F=L$. Obtain $E/L$, $\alpha$, $A\in\{0,1\}\subset k$, $B=b/\alpha^p$, $t=s/|\alpha|^p$ and a critical coset $C^\prime=B+S_{A,t}(E)$. The tame composition assertion makes $E/K$ finite tame. Hence the Frobenius-chain basis applies to $E/K$. It suffices to find a member of $C^\prime$ of norm $t$: normalization then descends it to $C$. The critical-coset calculus also gives $|A|\le t^{(p-1)/p}$ and $|pv|<t$ for every representative $v\in C^\prime$.

source.place: Propositions 6.2.4--6.2.5, printed pp. 43--44 and 47; Q23 normalization supplement.

proof.text: Approximate $B$ by a finite partial sum $v$ in the basis with $|B-v|<t$. Such a perturbation belongs to $S_{A,t}(E)$ by taking its $c$-term zero, so $v\in C^\prime$. Write $v=b_0+\sum_{j=0}^N\sum_u b_{ju}u^{p^j}$ with finite support, all coefficients in $k$. Orthogonality gives $|p b_{ju}u^{p^j}|\le|pv|<t$. If any representative already has norm $t$, stop.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.2.4, first paragraph, printed p. 47: finite-support approximation.

proof.text: For each term $q=b_{Nu}u^{p^N}$ of maximal level $N>0$, choose $d\in k$ with $d^p=b_{Nu}$ and set $c=d u^{p^{N-1}}$. Replace $v$ by $v-(c^p-Ac)$. This stays in the critical coset because $|pc^p|=|pq|<t$. It cancels $q$ and introduces only a level-$N-1$ term, since $A,d\in k$. Process the finitely many terms at level $N$, then descend in $N$; this terminates with $v=b_0+u_0$, $u_0\in\operatorname{Span}_k(U)$. At every stage the calculus preserves $|pv|<t$, so orthogonality justifies the next admissibility check.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.2.4, first paragraph, printed p. 47: descending Frobenius levels after coefficient normalization.

proof.text: Choose $d\in k$ with $d^p-Ad=b_0$. This uses algebraic closedness and $A\in k$. The coefficient bound implies $|d|^p\le\max(|b_0|,t)$: otherwise $|d|^p>|Ad|,|b_0|$, contradicting the equation. Since $|pb_0|\le|pv|<t$ and $|p|<1$, this gives $|pd^p|<t$. Subtract $d^p-Ad$, obtaining $u_0\in C^\prime\cap\operatorname{Span}_k(U)$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.2.4, printed p. 47: removal of the constant term, with admissibility written out.

proof.text: If $|u_0|>t$, the calculus gives $c\in E$ with $|pc^p|<t$ and $|u_0+c^p-Ac|<|u_0|$. Put $r=|c|^p$. If $r\le t$, the coefficient bound gives $|Ac|\le t$, impossible. Thus $r>t$ and $|Ac|<r$; cancellation forces $r=|u_0|$ and then $|u_0+c^p|<|u_0|$. This contradicts the power-orthogonality assertion of the basis node. Hence $|u_0|=t$. By Step 2 there is $w\in C$ with $|w|=s$. Write $w=b+c_0^p-ac_0+e$, $|e|<s$. The ultrametric inequality in both directions gives $|b+c_0^p-ac_0|=s$, proving the required unrestricted polynomial minimum.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.2.4, printed p. 47: final orthogonality argument; Lemma 6.1.2(i).

The worker's source gap is real: on p.47 the level-lowering term a·a_ij^{1/p}u^{p^{i-1}} and a_0=c^p-ac with c in k both need a in k. The new coefficient-normalization node repairs it correctly. I re-derived it: c=αy gives c^p-ac=α^p(y^p-y). E/F is Kummer of degree dividing p-1, hence tame. The normalized trace satisfies |T x|<=|x| and |T(x)^p-T(x^p)|<=|p||x|^p because n^{p-1}≡1 mod p, so it maps the extended coset into C without raising norms; this gives criticality and descent. The calculus node is faithful to Lemma 6.1.2 under nondiscreteness, plus the subgroup and translated-representative facts. The basis node is exactly Prop 6.2.5 including orthogonality to L^p. Item statement byte-identical to base. All six steps verified in detail: Step 1 nondiscreteness and completeness; Step 2 E/K tame by the composition clause of ramification-calculus; Step 3 finite approximation and the bound |pv|<t; Step 4 level-lowering uses A,d in k; Step 5 |d|^p<=max(|b_0|,t) by the coefficient bound; Step 6 the r<=t and r>t cases contradict power-orthogonality, then trace descent and removal of e. Edge cases a=0, p=2, L=K, type 2/3, equal and mixed characteristic.
